subject: SLA availability redlines, evidence request, and maintenance cutover coordination
content:
---- Message 1 (2028-05-16T09:12:00-07:00) ----
From: Alice Dawson <alice.dawson@orbitronics.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA targets for Orion pilot (Order Form attached)

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Orbitronics is excited to move the Orion pilot to a signed order. Before we sign, procurement and engineering have a couple of asks on the SLA and maintenance behavior we need clarified in the Order Form/MSA:

- Raise the uptime target to 99.95% for the pilot region (us-west).
- Cap service credits per month at a specific dollar amount rather than percentage; procurement will want a $10k monthly cap for pilot.
- Narrow maintenance windows to a 2-hour weekly window and require 48-hour advance notice for any emergency maintenance.
- Need evidence for incident postmortem timelines (SLA for RCA delivery) and a sample on-call rotation SOP.

I've attached a redlined Order Form (Orbitronics_OrderForm_v2_redline.docx) with inline comments where our legal/procurement expects changes. Please advise who on your side should own evidence artifacts and whether Redwood can provide a maintenance cutover runbook we can review.

Best,
Alice
Alice Dawson
Head of Platform Ops, Orbitronics
alice.dawson@orbitronics.com

Attachment: Orbitronics_OrderForm_v2_redline.docx (docx, 42 KB)

---- End Message 1 ----

---- Message 2 (2028-05-16T11:05:00-07:00) ----
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alice Dawson <alice.dawson@orbitronics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA targets for Orion pilot (Order Form attached)

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear notes and the redline. Looping in Laura (legal) and Connor (ops) to propose a path forward.

Quick responses to your bullets:
- Uptime target: we can discuss 99.95% for the pilot region, but need to align on measurement windows and exclusion carve-outs (partial-region failover). Laura will propose precise metric language.
- Credit cap: Redwood typically calculates credits as a percentage applied to monthly fees; we can accept a hard cap for pilot but need it reflected in the Order Form.
- Maintenance windows: ops comment required — Connor, can we support a 2-hour weekly window plus 48-hour notice for scheduled maintenance and a documented emergency process?
- Evidence: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), a sample incident postmortem template, and an ops runbook excerpt. Who should we send these artifacts to?

Proposed next steps:
1) Laura to send redline language for the MSA/SLA items by EOD.
2) Connor to attach the maintenance cutover runbook excerpt and a short note on emergency maintenance process.
3) Naomi will consolidate and share a single redlined Order Form + addendum for your procurement team.

Would you be available for a 30-min call tomorrow (Fri) to walk the procurement team through the proposed compromises?

Thanks,
Naomi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

---- End Message 2 ----

---- Message 3 (2028-05-16T14:30:00-07:00) ----
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Alice Dawson <alice.dawson@orbitronics.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA targets for Orion pilot (Order Form attached)

Hi all — I reviewed Orbitronics' redline and drafted targeted language that balances Orbitronics' asks with Redwood's operational realities. Key points below and attached redline (MSA_SLA_addendum_redline.docx):

- Availability metric: propose 99.95% measured over a monthly rolling window, with exclusions for force majeure, scheduled maintenance (as defined below), and customer-induced outages. Wording includes a cross-region clause in case partial-region traffic failover occurs.
- Service credits: we will accept a fixed credit cap for the pilot: credit calculation remains the percentage-of-monthly-fees model, but capped at $10,000 per calendar month for the pilot term.
- Maintenance windows: define "Standard Maintenance" as up to 2 hours per week with 48-hour notice for planned maintenance. "Emergency Maintenance" reserved for security-critical fixes; Redwood will provide as much notice as practicable and will notify affected customers within 1 hour of decision.
- RCA timeline: Redwood will provide an initial incident notification within 1 hour, a technical incident summary within 24 hours, and a formal RCA within 5 business days for Sev1 incidents. We can tighten this with an SLA credit trigger if Orbitronics requires but that will affect credit calculations.

I added inline comments where we need Orbitronics' procurement to confirm specific thresholds (e.g., what constitutes "affected customers" across multi-region deployments). If Orbitronics prefers an alternative cap or different RCA timing, indicate trade-offs in writing and we'll take that to exec legal review.

Attachment: MSA_SLA_addendum_redline.docx (docx, 28 KB)

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

---- End Message 3 ----

---- Message 4 (2028-05-17T09:00:00-07:00) ----
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Alice Dawson <alice.dawson@orbitronics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA targets for Orion pilot (Order Form attached)

Hi Alice / Naomi — ops here. A few operational clarifications and a short runbook excerpt attached (ops-runbook.pdf):

- Standard maintenance: We can support a 2-hour weekly window but ask that Orbitronics agree to a primary and fallback window (e.g., Tue 02:00–04:00 PT primary, Sun 03:00–05:00 PT fallback) to reduce customer-impact risk.
- Emergency maintenance: We will not take down control plane services without confirmation, but certain kernel/hypervisor patches require immediate host reboots. For those, we will provide an emergency bulletin and attempt live migration where possible.
- Cutover rehearsal: For the pilot, we recommend a single coordinated cutover rehearsal with Orbitronics engineers before any production maintenance freeze; this reduces rollout surprises.
- Evidence artifacts: I can provide a sanitized incident postmortem template, on-call rotation schedule template, and a small excerpt of our runbook. See ops-runbook.pdf.

Connor O'Brien
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

Attachment: ops-runbook.pdf (pdf, 112 KB)

---- End Message 4 ----

---- Message 5 (2028-05-17T10:25:00-07:00) ----
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alice Dawson <alice.dawson@orbitronics.com>, procurement@orbitronics.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA targets for Orion pilot (Order Form attached)

Hi Alice — great discussion so far. To summarize the compromises we're proposing for the pilot:

- Availability: 99.95% monthly rolling; exclusions listed in the addendum.
- Credits: percentage-based credit calculation, capped at $10,000/month for pilot term.
- Maintenance: 2-hour weekly standard window with defined primary+fallback windows; 48-hour notice for planned maintenance, emergency process described in addendum.
- RCA: initial notification 1 hour, technical summary 24 hours, formal RCA within 5 business days for Sev1.

Next steps I propose:
1) Orbitronics confirms acceptance of the above compromises and returns the redlined Order Form (or suggests any final numeric tweaks).
2) If accepted, we will issue the final combined redline and send a DocuSign link for signature.
3) Connor to deliver the cutover rehearsal checklist and evidence artifacts to alice.dawson@orbitronics.com.

I attached the combined redline (MSA_SLA_addendum_redline.docx and Orbitronics_OrderForm_v2_redline.docx consolidated) — if procurement is happy, I can send the DocuSign envelope today. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/CR-ORION-7890

Thanks,
Naomi

Attachment: MSA_SLA_addendum_redline.docx (docx, 28 KB); Orbitronics_OrderForm_v2_redline.docx (docx, 42 KB)

---- End Message 5 ----

---- Message 6 (2028-05-18T15:32:00-07:00) ----
From: Alice Dawson <alice.dawson@orbitronics.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orbitronics.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 18 May 2028 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA targets for Orion pilot (Order Form attached)

Naomi — thanks, that all looks reasonable. Procurement confirms the $10k cap for the pilot and engineering is good with the 2-hour weekly window + primary/fallback. A couple of small asks before signature:

- Please include the cutover rehearsal checklist in the DocuSign package or as a supporting artifact.
- Can we get the sanitized SOC 2 cover page and a sample Sev1 RCA? (redacted)

I've attached our PO (PO_Orbitronics_20280518.pdf) so finance can start pre-approval. We can take a 30-min wrap-up call Monday afternoon if that helps. Otherwise please send the DocuSign link and we'll finalize.

Best,
Alice
Alice Dawson
Head of Platform Ops, Orbitronics

Attachment: PO_Orbitronics_20280518.pdf (pdf, 15 KB)

---- End Message 6 ----
